item.evidence: projects.py:191-195 commits the project update before :203 inserts its snapshot; :185-189 lets a concurrent saver backfill the new current version using snapshot(project) with the default empty note. :204-205 swallows all snapshot insert exceptions. Restore similarly updates at :240-243 and swallows snapshot failure at :247-250. The uniqueness constraint is server.py:77 on (project_id, version).
item.expected: R-191: saves "write [the note] onto the snapshot they create"; R-177: restore "creates a new newest version" and "leaves every earlier version intact"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure." Preserve the submitted note and snapshot alongside every acknowledged version.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a successful save can permanently lose its version note. After A commits v2 but before its snapshot insert, B can read v2, backfill it with an empty note, and advance to v3; A's unique-key failure is silently swallowed. A sees Saved v2, but history never shows A's explanation. Separately, a failed post-update snapshot write is acknowledged on save/restore and can leave that saved version inaccessible to history/restore. Users cannot repair the missing note through the label-only UI; existing current system data remains available. These are source-backed interleavings, not runtime observations.
reproduction_steps: Owner/editor A saves v2 with note 'Before boss fight rework'.
Before A's snapshot insert, editor B reads v2 and saves v3; B's pre-save backfill creates the v2 snapshot with no note.
A's snapshot insert conflicts and is ignored; open Compare → History and observe the predicted blank v2 note despite A's successful save.
Alternatively, encounter a snapshot insert failure after a save/restore commit: the endpoint still reports success without that version being in history.
item.surface: Save with version note; Restore version; Compare → History
item.title: Acknowledged saves can lose their notes or history entries — snapshot writes race after the project commit and failures are ignored

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:455 awaits restore for the current project, but :458-459 unconditionally setProject(meta) and openSystem(system, context). item.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: preserve "context restoration ... return paths". Restoring A should not replace a different project opened while A's request was pending.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: an owner/editor restoring project A can open project B while the request is slow. The late A response switches the workspace back to A and clears B's unsynthesized inputs via openSystem, without confirmation. B's saved copy remains recoverable by reopening it, but edits made during that interval are lost. The source proves the overwrite branch; no network timing was executed.
reproduction_steps: Open project A → Compare → select v1 → Restore v1.
While its request is pending, open B from Projects and type a synthesis note or adjust dials.
When A's response arrives, source predicts A replaces B and B's queued edits disappear.
item.surface: Compare → Restore vN while opening another project
item.title: A slow restore replaces a different project opened afterward — restore applies its response without an identity guard

item.evidence: projects.py:215 sorts descending and calls to_list(1000) with no pagination or truncation metadata; Workspace.jsx:478-479 puts only that array into versions; :522-523 and HistoryModal.jsx:9 render that array as all saved versions. Reload to obtain the correct zero.

item.evidence: zipExport.js:13-15 extracts only class/struct identifiers; :225 adds sibling dependencies only when such an identifier appears in the consumer code. It does not inspect sibling #include paths or DECLARE_*DELEGATE names. :254 passes only p.uses to writeModule, which writes those dependencies at :164-167.
item.expected: R-187: "copying the folder ... installs every selected system together"; R-208: required engine dependencies and request: "with its own module files, so it installs with no code edits"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: trace structure and dependencies through to usable output. A consumer that includes a sibling module's public header needs that sibling in Build.cs, even if it uses only a delegate declared there.

The bundler never recognizes that as using HealthKit, so StaminaKit.Build.cs lacks HealthKit and Unreal cannot resolve the sibling public header on its module include path. Bundling valid interoperating systems therefore requires manual Build.cs edits. This is a source-predicted dependency omission; no exported plugin was compiled.
reproduction_steps: Have a Health project with HealthComponent.generated.h, UHealthComponent and a macro-declared FOnHealthChanged delegate.
Have a Stamina project whose code includes HealthComponent.h and uses FOnHealthChanged without referencing UHealthComponent.
Bundle both projects and inspect StaminaKit.Build.cs.
HealthKit is absent; add it manually to make the sibling public include available.
item.surface: Projects → Bundle plugin → sibling module dependency planning
item.title: Bundles omit dependencies used only through sibling headers or delegates — dependency planning matches class names rather than includes

Distinct project ids remain distinct even if their mutable names match. The later request "Warn, but still allow export" supersedes only blocking, not detection.

Other warnings may still appear (including the artificial mutual dependency inferred from the repeated class), but the actionable duplicate-class diagnosis and its rename fix are omitted. The user must inspect code or interpret less-specific warnings; export is intentionally still allowed and no project is modified.

Select both and open Bundle plugin.
Source predicts no 'both declare UHealthComponent' conflict because the stored display names are equal, although separate modules are planned.
item.surface: Projects → Bundle plugin → Conflicts between systems
item.title: Duplicate-class diagnostics omit conflicts between projects with the same name — display labels are used as project identity
